clue.text: Like a desert island clothed, say, in rolling dune

indicators.note: something rolling tumbles over, so the letters turn into a new order
one piece sits in the middle of the jumbled one

blocks.note: taken as written, then jumbled and split around the other piece
a nun dressed in her robe is in habit; 'say' flags the example

explanation.surface: A castaway's island, sand dunes everywhere, with someone dressed among them.
explanation.definitionFit: A desert island has nobody living on it, so it is empty of residents.

clue.text: Minced tuna enticed? Not tried

indicators.note: minced food is chopped up, so these letters are chopped into a new order

explanation.surface: Chopped-up tuna offered as bait to lure a cat, which ignores it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something never attempted has never been tried at all.

clue.text: What's initially sported by Islamic haji residing at Mecca?

definitions.text: What's initially sported by Islamic haji residing at Mecca?

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each following word

blocks.note: first letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: Asking what a pilgrim to Mecca first puts on when he arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition. A haji is a Muslim pilgrim to Mecca, and the ihram is the simple white garment worn on that pilgrimage.
explanation.definitionFit: The ihram is the plain white pilgrim dress worn in the sacred state at Mecca during hajj.

clue.text: Non-orthodox call for attention gets habitual response

definitions.note: adjective; heretic is used as an adjective, more often heretical

blocks.note: 'Here!' is a shout to make someone look
a tic is an involuntary habitual twitch

explanation.surface: Someone shouting to be noticed earns only a reflex twitch in reply.
explanation.definitionFit: A heretic holds beliefs departing from accepted religious doctrine, hence unorthodox.

clue.text: Rejection, but not concerning enthusiast

indicators.note: but not says the first word is wanted without the following one

blocks.note: a rebuff is a curt rejection
re means concerning, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: A refusal that has nothing to do with a fan.
explanation.definitionFit: A film buff or wine buff is a keen devotee of that subject.

clue.text: Attempt holding one small container — it's a tiny thing

indicators.note: the attempt word holds the next pieces inside it

blocks.note: a vial is a small bottle

explanation.surface: Trying to grip a single little bottle, a minor matter.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A triviality is a trifle, something of little importance or size.

clue.text: Anomalistic die needs reworking for conversion to metric

indicators.note: reworking means remaking, so the letters are rebuilt into a new order

explanation.surface: A strangely behaving die must be remade to suit a changed measuring system.
explanation.walkthrough: Britain's switch to decimal currency in 1971 was called decimalisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Decimalisation is moving a currency or measures onto a base-ten system, as with metric units.

clue.text: Bottom's tender — essential having a doctor over to look at daughter

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the doctor abbreviation is read backwards

blocks.note: to see is to look at
D abbreviates daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A sore backside needs a doctor brought round to examine the daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottom is the weaver in A Midsummer Night's Dream, not a body part; the fairy Mustardseed waits on him when Titania dotes on him.
explanation.definitionFit: Mustardseed is one of the fairies told by Titania to attend and serve Bottom in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Second, not first number is samey

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a second
one is the first counting number

explanation.surface: Coming second rather than first in the numbering makes no difference.
explanation.definitionFit: Monotone describes something unvarying and dull, lacking variety in tone.

clue.text: Keep quiet about your area's grape variety

indicators.note: about means going round, so the quiet word surrounds the rest

blocks.note: YR is a written abbreviation of your

explanation.surface: Someone tells you to stay quiet about the grape grown where you live.
explanation.definitionFit: Syrah, also called Shiraz, is a dark-skinned red wine grape.

clue.text: Relax, with everything mostly consumed around six

definitions.note: verb in the sense of ease

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter goes
around places the shortened word round the numeral

explanation.surface: Unwinding after eating almost everything at about six o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: Relax looks like resting, but here it means easing a pain.
explanation.definitionFit: To alleviate pain or worry is to ease or relax it, making it less severe.

clue.text: Lust is urgent outside English society

indicators.note: the urgent word sits outside, wrapping the other two pieces

blocks.note: a dire need is an urgent one

explanation.surface: Passion is pressing beyond the bounds of polite English company.
explanation.definitionFit: Desire as a noun means strong sexual longing, the sense of lust.

clue.text: Famous Australian statesmen offering title for Lytton Strachey

blocks.note: people of the Australian state of Victoria

explanation.surface: Renowned Australian politicians supply the name of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a biography of Australians; Strachey's 1918 book in fact debunked four great figures of Queen Victoria's Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminent Victorians is the 1918 collection of four irreverent biographical essays written by Lytton Strachey.

clue.text: Designer including small and short homage for wholesaler

indicators.note: including means the designer's name takes the other pieces inside it
short says the word is cut off before its final letter

blocks.note: abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A fashion house pays a little tribute to the trade middleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A distributor is a middleman supplying goods in bulk to retailers, as a wholesaler does.

clue.text: What uses moving trail icon for craft?

definitions.text: What uses moving trail icon for craft?

indicators.note: moving letters are shifted about into a new order

explanation.surface: A riddle about whoever follows moving trail markers for aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: the controllers watch each aircraft as a moving icon trailing across a radar screen.
explanation.definitionFit: Air traffic controllers track planes as blips on radar screens and direct them safely.

clue.text: European whiskey is on board

indicators.note: on board means placed inside a vessel, so the pieces sit within it

blocks.note: SS, steamship, stands for the vessel one is aboard
whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man from the Continent has a drink on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: On board conventionally means inside SS, the steamship abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swiss person is a native of Switzerland, a country of Europe.

clue.text: Returning bird loses minutes eating a fruit

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the bird's name runs backwards
loses tells us one letter is dropped
eating means taking something inside

blocks.note: the motmot is a tropical American bird

explanation.surface: A bird flies back and wastes no time pecking at a fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: TOMTOM loses one M to give TOMTO, which then takes A inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The tomato is botanically a fruit, a berry of the nightshade plant.

clue.text: Is game of football pursuing male conflict?

indicators.note: pursuing means coming after, so the male letter stands in front

blocks.note: a football game is a match

explanation.surface: Is a football fixture really about men fighting?
explanation.definitionFit: A mismatch is an incompatibility or clash between two things that do not fit.

clue.text: Sudden change of opinion about English marine artist

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the change word goes round the others

blocks.note: to veer is to swing suddenly in direction or view

explanation.surface: A sudden U-turn about an English painter of the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The marine and English pieces sit inside in reverse clue order. 'Marine artist' suggests a seascape painter, but marine belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Johannes Vermeer was the Dutch Golden Age painter of interiors such as Girl with a Pearl Earring.

clue.text: Footballers, say, introducing new underpants

indicators.note: introducing means bringing something in, so a letter goes inside

blocks.note: footballers are examples of people who kick

explanation.surface: Footballers showing off a new line of underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain knickers are women's underpants.
explanation.definitionFit: Knickers is the everyday British word for women's or girls' underpants.

clue.text: Florentine family, note, nearly all like a lot of drugs

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A Renaissance dynasty's letter notes that most of them were like users of drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Many drugs are medicinal, having healing properties and used to treat illness.

clue.text: Tactful beginning of play 'The Ambassadors'?

blocks.note: in tennis the service starts each point

explanation.surface: A tactful opening night for a play called The Ambassadors.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make it look like a play title (Henry James wrote a novel of that name); here it is just the ambassadors as a body.
explanation.definitionFit: The diplomatic service is the branch of government staffing embassies abroad, made up of ambassadors.

clue.text: Assistant ref's backing nothing — means one needs to replace

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the zero word is reversed
to re-place is to place again in a different order

blocks.note: nil is a football score of nothing

explanation.surface: A referee supporting a goalless result means someone must stand in.
explanation.definitionFit: A linesman is a match official who assists the referee from the touchline in football.

clue.text: Direction: the French must replace old Maigret?

indicators.note: must replace says one piece goes where another stood

explanation.surface: A director's note: a French actor will replace the old Maigret.
explanation.definitionFit: Maigret is Simenon's fictional Paris police detective, an example of a sleuth.

clue.text: Try second dose of drugs

blocks.note: a tab is a tablet, one dose

explanation.surface: Attempting a second helping of medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Stab is an informal noun for an attempt, as in the idiom have a go.

clue.text: Like rugby side that's lost player, unable to leave the ground?

definitions.text: Like rugby side that's lost player

blocks.clueFragment: Like rugby side that's lost player
blocks.note: first meaning: a team missing one of its wing players
second meaning: like a bird or insect that cannot fly

explanation.walkthrough: Ground suggests the rugby pitch; here it is the earth, which a creature without wings cannot rise from.
explanation.definitionFit: Without wings a team lacks its wide players, and a creature lacks the means of flight.

clue.text: Finally put sword in mobile cover

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the next word

blocks.note: the epee is a fencing sword

explanation.surface: At last sheathing a sword inside a portable case.
explanation.definitionFit: A tepee is a conical tent of hide or canvas, a shelter that can be moved.

clue.text: Concluding race unable to be seen regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: a race is an event at an athletics meeting

explanation.surface: A final race that cannot be watched at regular intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventual means coming at the end of a process, ultimate or final.

clue.text: Very pretty trim, easy to remove small area

indicators.note: to remove means the letter for the area is taken out

explanation.surface: A neat haircut that is simple to take off a small patch.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutesy means cute in an overdone, sugary way, excessively pretty.

clue.text: Scientist has info to quote over mist obscuring motorway

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the quote word is read backwards
the mist hides the motorway, which disappears from view

blocks.note: British motorways are numbered M1, M25 and so on

explanation.surface: A researcher passes on a travel report about fog on the motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A geneticist is a scientist who studies genes and heredity.

clue.text: Volume of church in French capital, hard to take in

blocks.note: Paris is the capital of France
H is the pencil grade for hard
to register a fact is to take it in

explanation.definitionFit: A parish register is the book recording the baptisms, marriages and burials in a parish church.

clue.text: Old Greek perishes after eating melon

indicators.note: having eaten something means holding it inside

blocks.note: the ogen is a variety of melon

explanation.surface: An ancient Greek dies after eating a melon.
explanation.walkthrough: The ogen is a small sweet melon first bred in Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: Diogenes was the ancient Greek Cynic philosopher said to have lived in a large jar.

clue.text: Lift high frequency in faster military jet

indicators.note: in places the frequency letters inside the word for faster

blocks.note: to lift is slang for to steal

explanation.surface: A plane climbing on a high radio frequency in a quicker jet.
explanation.walkthrough: Faster here means more firmly held, not quicker, so it gives TIGHTER.

clue.text: Northern company is after light dance music

indicators.note: after means coming behind, so these pieces follow the light

clue.text: British species of tree — little ones

blocks.note: Abies is the botanical name of the fir genus

explanation.surface: A British tree variety, with small ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Little ones is an affectionate phrase for young children or infants.

clue.text: Weird set of images apt with a Ngaio Marsh novel?

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: A detective story by Ngaio Marsh full of strange visions.
explanation.walkthrough: Ngaio Marsh was a New Zealand crime writer, so 'novel' looks like one of her books.
explanation.definitionFit: A phantasmagoria is a bizarre dreamlike sequence of shifting images.

clue.text: Decorative glass item? Mirror, perhaps, with a number

blocks.note: the Daily Mirror is an example of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A looking glass, maybe, with a numeral, as a decorative glass object.
explanation.walkthrough: Mirror looks like the glass item, but it is the British tabloid.

clue.text: Act offensively in an instance of shooting wild rams

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters run into a new order

blocks.note: in film-making each shot is a take

explanation.surface: Going on the attack by shooting at untamed rams.

clue.text: From CI on a reading to east, you agree?

blocks.note: the letters C and I spoken as words

explanation.surface: Reading from a Channel Islands source eastwards, do you concur?
explanation.walkthrough: CI looks like the Channel Islands abbreviation, but it is just two letters to be said.
explanation.definitionFit: To see eye to eye is the idiom for two people agreeing completely.

blocks.note: to manage a business is to run it

explanation.definitionFit: A countryman is a person who lives in the country rather than in town.

clue.text: Unusually phallic tie, perhaps related to something on French letter?

definitions.text: related to something on French letter?

indicators.note: unusually means not in the usual form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rude-shaped necktie, and a nudge towards a French letter.

explanation.definitionFit: Philatelic means to do with stamp collecting, and a stamp is what sits on a letter.

clue.text: Elder gave out in flooded marsh

indicators.note: out means wrong or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A senior person handed things round in a waterlogged swamp.
explanation.definitionFit: An everglade is a tract of swampy grassland, best known from the Florida Everglades.

indicators.note: on the phone a word is only heard, not seen written

explanation.surface: Ordering sweets by phone.
explanation.walkthrough: Chews are a kind of chewy sweet in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonyms: both verbs mean picking one option out from several available.

blocks.note: hale means healthy, as in hale and hearty

explanation.surface: A sunflower's seed head as a healthy origin of cooking oil.

clue.text: Month before girl's producing short stories

blocks.note: Ella's, possessive of a girl's name

clue.text: Precipitate of arsenic introduced to rhodium

explanation.walkthrough: Precipitate looks like the chemistry noun; it is the adjective meaning hasty.

clue.text: Key European manuscript with character is a precious jewel

blocks.note: the tone of a place is its character

clue.text: Continuing with ringing sounds after bishops leave

clue.text: Heartless sectarian in charge of life

blocks.note: a sectarian is a narrow-minded bigot

clue.text: Book followed by clergyman, one with key lines?

definitions.text: Book followed by clergyman, one with key lines?

explanation.surface: A prayer book read by a priest, full of set lines.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is wordplay and also a picture of the answer: a prayer book whose set lines a priest reads through.

clue.text: Black, like house poet

blocks.note: B is the pencil grade for black

explanation.surface: A dark poet, as gloomy as a house in mourning.

blocks.note: to get something is to have it

clue.text: Utter greatness resulting in star quality

explanation.surface: Total grandeur produces celebrity charisma.

explanation.definitionFit: Absolute magnitude is an astronomical measure of a star's intrinsic brightness.
